country.name: Cameroon
country.coastline: Atlantic (Gulf of Guinea / Bight of Biafra)
country.summary: Cameroon is the maritime gateway of the CEMAC hinterland: roughly 80% of Central Africa's transit traffic moves on the two rail/road corridors from Douala to N'Djamena (Chad) and Bangui (CAR), and about 79% of Chad's imports enter through Douala. National port traffic was 26.9m tonnes in 2024, split mainly between the historic river port of Douala (12.9m t, container terminal run by the state-owned RTC since Bolloré/APM Terminals' DIT concession ended in 2020) and the Chinese-built deep-sea port of Kribi (12.7m t, 16 m draft), whose second container terminal opened in May 2025 and lifted capacity to about 1m TEU under an AGL/CMA CGM/CHEC concession. Headline projects are the 4,000 ha Kribi Port Industrial Zone (EUR 795m, AGL/Arise IIP/Belmont, launched Feb 2026), the World Bank-financed Cameroon–Chad corridor programme (Douala–Yaoundé rail rehabilitation, Ngaoundéré intermodal platform), phase 2 of the Yaoundé–Douala motorway, the Kribi–Lolabé motorway and a still-unfunded Limbe deep-sea port for which MSC's TIL opened talks in July 2026. DP World has no asset in Cameroon; the market is dominated by AGL (MSC), CMA CGM, CHEC and ICTSI, with state-run RTC at Douala.

ports.name: Port of Douala-Bonabéri
ports.operator: Port Autonome de Douala (PAD, state landlord); container terminal: Régie du Terminal à Conteneurs (RTC, PAD-owned, since 1 Jan 2020); timber yard: Bolloré/AGL group; security: Douala Port Security (DPS/PortSec SA)
ports.concession: Container terminal was concessioned in 2005 for 15 years to Douala International Terminal (DIT, Bolloré + APM Terminals), which invested CFA 43.4bn; the state refused renewal and evicted DIT in Dec 2020, handing operations to the in-house RTC. DIT won ICC arbitration and a Paris Court of Appeal ruling (Jan 2023) against PAD over the eviction.
ports.capacity: River port on the Wouri estuary; ~8 m alongside depth, max ~200 m LOA (tidal/dredging constrained); container terminal 660 m of quay, 3 berths; RTC targets 1m TEU/year capacity by 2026 after extension
ports.throughput: 12.92m tonnes (2024, +6% vs 12.19m t in 2023); container TEU figure n/a (RTC handled ~3,000 boxes/week in 2024); transit traffic passed 500,000 t in Q1 2026
ports.projects: RTC container-terminal extension awarded Dec 2022 to Negri (CFA 47.2bn): +250 m quay, 7.9 ha backfill, 1,200 m roadways, target ≥1,000 m linear quay; 8 RTG cranes (CFA 12bn) delivered from Nov 2023; RTC invested >CFA 44bn 2020-23; Navis N4 TOS. World Bank Cameroon-Chad corridor project (approved Feb 2022) rehabilitates the Douala–Yaoundé rail link and Bessengue rail platform serving the port.
ports.notes: Cameroon's main gateway and the historic entry point for Chad and CAR transit; industrial land in the port is reported at 100% occupancy. Draft limits container-ship size, so Kribi increasingly relays boxes to Douala by feeder (about 30% of Kribi's transshipment flows to/from Douala). Competitor context: former Bolloré/APMT concession renationalised; no DP World presence.

ports.name: Kribi Deep-Sea Port (Port Autonome de Kribi)
ports.operator: Port Autonome de Kribi (PAK, landlord); Kribi Conteneurs Terminal (KCT: Africa Global Logistics/ex-Bolloré lead, CMA CGM, CHEC, Cameroonian investors incl. Belmont/Colin Mukete); Kribi Multipurpose Terminal (KMT: ICTSI-led consortium)
ports.concession: KCT container concession (Bolloré/CMA CGM/CHEC) operating since March 2018, phase-2 amendment signed 26 Sep 2022; KMT multipurpose concession (ICTSI) in commercial operation since Oct 2020; terms n/a
ports.capacity: Draft 16 m; terminal 1: 350 m quay, ~300,000 TEU/yr; terminal 2 (opened 9 May 2025): 715 m quay, 30-33 ha yard, 5 STS cranes (65 t), 15 yard cranes — total container capacity ~1m TEU/yr (PAK cites 1.2m TEU); breakwater extended by 675 m; can receive 400 m 'megamax' ships (MSC Turkiye, May 2025)
ports.throughput: 12.7m tonnes (2024, vs 10.7m t in 2023); KCT ~750,000 TEU in first 12 months after terminal 2 opening (May 2025-May 2026, +82%), ~74,000 TEU in March 2025, ~70% transshipment; PAK revenue CFA 35.3bn (2024, +24%), net profit CFA 4bn (2025)
ports.projects: Phase 2 (CFA 400bn, 75% China Eximbank, built by CHEC) delivered 2025; KCT invested CFA 70bn in terminal-2 equipment (2024); KCT preparing an 8 ha yard extension to reach 1.2m TEU/yr and discussing phase 3 (quay extension); PAK plans a mineral (iron ore/bauxite) terminal from 2027 and a hydrocarbons/LNG terminal from 2028; 26,000 ha master plan to 2040 (CFA 6,500bn); standard-gauge railway from Mbalam/Nabeba iron ore mines under construction (2025)
ports.notes: Only deep-water port in the CEMAC zone; positioned by MSC/AGL as the Gulf of Guinea transshipment hub on the Asia–West Africa 'Africa Express' loop (80% of flows via Singapore). Competitor concession: AGL (MSC) + CMA CGM + CHEC at KCT, ICTSI at KMT. Adjacent Kome-Kribi 1 FSO is the marine outlet of the Chad–Cameroon oil pipeline (since 2003). No DP World presence.

ports.name: Port of Limbe (existing port and Limbe Deep Seaport project)
ports.operator: Port Autonome de Limbe / Limbe Port Authority (state); existing traffic dominated by SONARA refinery hydrocarbons (Limboh terminal) and an oil-services yard
ports.concession: n/a — government held a first working session with Terminal Investment Limited (TIL, MSC group) on 15 July 2026 to explore a PPP to develop, modernise and operate the future deep seaport; a July 2025 MoU with Turkish contractor Yenigün was announced then postponed
ports.capacity: Existing: ~750 m of berthing, 5 warehouses, petroleum products/timber/cement; deep-seaport project budgeted at ~CFA 400bn (~USD 667m) in government programming documents
ports.throughput: Limbe traffic fell 957,162 t (-23%) in 2024 (national port statistics); absolute figure n/a
ports.projects: Limbe Deep Seaport: feasibility studies 2009 (updated since), dedicated port authority created, project delayed for over a decade; TIL/MSC exploratory talks July 2026; Idenau and Tiko incorporated in the Limbe port authority's remit; MAGZI plans a 1,000 ha industrial zone at Limbe by 2035
ports.notes: South-West region port 15 nautical miles from Douala, oriented to Nigeria trade and oil services; existing traffic is largely SONARA-related and has been hit by the refinery's 2019 fire and Anglophone-region insecurity. Prospective competitor concession: TIL (MSC). Opportunity: no terminal operator selected yet.

ports.name: Port of Tiko
ports.operator: State (now placed under the Limbe port authority together with Idenau)
ports.capacity: Two docks totalling ~300 m; historically ~29,000 t/yr; creek port for coastal/regional vessels
ports.projects: n/a — included in the Limbe deep-seaport perimeter
ports.notes: Small agro-export port (bananas, rubber, palm oil, timber, cocoa) serving CDC plantations; informal coastal trade with Nigeria (Calabar). Marginal for international operators.

ports.name: Garoua River Port (Bénoué)
ports.operator: Garoua Urban Community (transferred 2003); management committee set up 2 April 2026 under the Bénoué prefect
ports.capacity: Two 250 m docks, ~6 m depth, 12,000 m² stockyard; navigable only June–October (Bénoué high water); silting
ports.throughput: n/a — no regular commercial traffic, mainly artisanal pirogues (2020-24 audit noted uncollected port fees)
ports.projects: Rehabilitation/modernisation estimated at CFA 16bn (financing to be found); government wants to move from studies to execution; a second dry port is also planned at Garoua
ports.notes: Historic river link to Nigeria via the Bénoué/Niger; relevance today is cross-border trade with Nigeria and Chad rather than sea access. Low priority for private terminal operators.

ports.name: Kome-Kribi 1 marine terminal (Chad–Cameroon pipeline FSO)
ports.operator: COTCO (Cameroon Oil Transportation Company) – Chad–Cameroon pipeline consortium
ports.capacity: Offshore FSO loading tankers above 300,000 DWT
ports.notes: Export outlet of the 1,070 km Chad–Cameroon pipeline (Doba fields); other oil terminals: Limboh (SONARA, Limbe), Kole, Ebome (Perenco), Moudi.

zones.name: Kribi Port Industrial Zone (KPIZ)
zones.authority: Port Autonome de Kribi (PAK) with consortium Africa Global Logistics (MSC), Arise Integrated Industrial Platforms and Belmont Investments (Colin Mukete); financiers AfDB, EU Global Gateway, IFC
zones.area: 4,000 ha (MAGZI separately projects 5,000 ha of industrial land at Kribi by 2035)
zones.incentives: Cameroon economic-zone / industrial free-zone regime (details n/a); phased sectoral clusters (heavy/medium industry, food processing, R&D)
zones.tenants: ~CFA 400bn already invested 2018-2025 by industrial operators in cocoa processing, cement, flour milling and logistics
zones.projects: Total EUR 795m (~CFA 521bn); first phase EUR 400m; Tanger Med Special Agency withdrew from the consortium before launch
zones.notes: Flagship port-linked SEZ of Central Africa; developer consortium led by MSC's AGL and Arise IIP (Gabon GSEZ model) — a direct competitor platform to DP World's economic-zone offering.

zones.name: Kribi port logistics and industrial zone (PAK port domain)
zones.area: 1,200 ha under phased development to 2027; +30 ha storage yard added in phase II
zones.tenants: KCT (AGL/CMA CGM/CHEC), KMT (ICTSI) one-stop service centre, logistics operators
zones.projects: Specialised aluminium, bauxite, hydrocarbon and LNG terminals planned; mineral terminal construction from 2027, hydrocarbons terminal 2028
zones.notes: Inside the 26,000 ha Kribi port complex master plan; feeds the wider KPIZ.

zones.name: Douala-Bassa Industrial Zone (MAGZI)
zones.authority: MAGZI (Mission d'Aménagement et de Gestion des Zones Industrielles, state)
zones.incentives: Serviced industrial land leased by MAGZI; general Cameroon investment-incentive law (2013) applies
zones.tenants: 89 industrial units (about 25% of Douala's industrial output); Douala's two MAGZI zones host ~160 firms
zones.projects: MAGZI plans 300 ha at Yassa (Douala east) and 500 ha at Dibombari by 2035
zones.notes: Saturated legacy zone next to the port and Camrail's Bassa workshops; land disputes and expulsions of non-compliant tenants reported. MAGZI's 11 zones total 1,293 ha with 405 firms nationally.

zones.name: Douala-Bonabéri Industrial Zone (MAGZI)
zones.incentives: MAGZI serviced land lease; national investment-incentive regime
zones.tenants: n/a (part of ~160 firms across Douala's two MAGZI zones)
zones.notes: West-bank zone adjacent to the Bonabéri port sector and the Wouri bridge; road access to the North-West/West regions.

zones.name: Ngaoundéré rail/road platform and dry port
zones.authority: Camrail terminal operated by SMN (Société de Manutention de Ngaoundéré); dry-port project led by Ministry of Transport
zones.area: Dry port: ~200 ha allocated at Beka Matari; existing Camrail container terminal capacity 1,350 TEU
zones.opened: n/a (rail terminal operational since railway completion in 1974)
zones.projects: Dry-port project (announced 2022, budget ~CFA 1.4bn, studies and tender) still without a firm start date; rehabilitation of the Ngaoundéré rail/road platform is a component of the World Bank Cameroon-Chad corridor project (2026 work plan)
zones.notes: Rail-head of the Douala–N'Djamena corridor where rail freight (roughly 39% modal share Douala–Ngaoundéré, 90% for fuel) shifts to trucks for Chad; a Chad-owned dry port on 10 ha downstream of Douala port (GPM/Genesis) has also been mooted.

zones.name: Edéa industrial zone
zones.authority: MAGZI (planned extension); existing industry anchored by Alucam smelter and the Edéa hydropower plant
zones.tenants: Alucam aluminium smelter and related industries (existing, outside MAGZI perimeter)
zones.projects: Part of MAGZI's 9,101 ha programme to 2035; Edéa sits at the junction of the Douala–Yaoundé motorway phase 2 (Edéa Est–Edéa Ouest section) and the Edéa–Kribi motorway
zones.notes: Strategic node between Douala, Yaoundé and Kribi; financing of MAGZI zones is the main constraint (only CFA 20bn mobilised in ~50 years).

zones.name: Garoua-Boulaï truck logistics hub (CNCC)
zones.authority: Conseil National des Chargeurs du Cameroun (CNCC)
zones.area: 2+ ha; parking for 200 trucks, accommodation, restaurant, admin block, borehole and generator
zones.projects: Fourth CNCC logistics base under construction at Kousséri (Chad border); earlier bases at Dibamba (Douala) and Ngoulentang
zones.notes: Secures the border staging area for CAR-bound convoys; customs values goods transiting this route at ~CFA 55bn/year.

zones.name: Ombé industrial zone (Limbe/Tiko) and planned Limbe 1,000 ha zone
zones.area: n/a (existing Ombé zone); 1,000 ha new zone at Limbe planned by 2035
zones.projects: 1,000 ha Limbe industrial zone tied to the Limbe deep-seaport project
zones.notes: Only MAGZI zone in the South-West region; activity constrained by the Anglophone crisis since 2017.

corridors.name: Douala – Yaoundé – Ngaoundéré – Kousséri – N'Djamena corridor (Cameroon–Chad)
corridors.route: Port of Douala → Yaoundé → Bélabo → Ngaoundéré (rail, ~900 km) → Garoua → Maroua → Kousséri/Nguéli bridge → N'Djamena (road); road-only variant via Ngaoundéré–Garoua–Kousséri
corridors.length: ~1,800 km Douala–N'Djamena (rail ~885 km to Ngaoundéré + ~900 km road)
corridors.operator: Camrail (AGL) for rail; road trucking mainly by Chadian/Cameroonian hauliers; CNCC/BGFT corridor management
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: ~79% of Chad's imports transit via Douala; ~CFA 340-350bn of Chadian goods per year; Camrail carried 1.8m t of freight in 2014 (>2/3 of Chad's imports by rail then); rail modal share Douala–Ngaoundéré ~39% (90% for petroleum)
corridors.projects: World Bank Cameroon-Chad Transport Corridor project (P167798, approved 15 Feb 2022, ~USD 495-816m incl. IDA USD 345m; effective June 2024): Douala–Yaoundé rail rehabilitation and signalling (USD 368m), Ngaoundéré rail/road platform, N'Djamena–Moundou road, trade facilitation; 2026 rail budget CFA 11.12bn. EU/EIB Global Gateway: rehabilitation of 229 km of the 596 km N'Djamena–Koutéré–Moundou road (works from Q2 2024). Yagoua–Bongor Logone bridge (CFA 74bn, AfDB + EU EUR 40m) opened 28 Apr 2025. AfDB Transport Facilitation Programme (2007, UA 454m) built Garoua-Boulaï–Ngaoundéré and Kousséri sections.
corridors.notes: Backbone of Central African transit (with Douala–Bangui, ~80% of the sub-region's transit traffic); insecurity in the Far North (Boko Haram) and truck convoys add time/cost; Kribi increasingly competes for Chad-bound containers via Douala feeders and road. Camrail concession (AGL) is the key competitor asset on the rail leg.

corridors.name: Douala – Yaoundé – Bertoua – Garoua-Boulaï/Béloko – Bangui corridor (Cameroon–CAR)
corridors.route: Port of Douala (or Kribi) → Yaoundé → Bertoua (or rail to Bélabo) → Garoua-Boulaï → Béloko (CAR) → Bouar → Bangui
corridors.operator: Road hauliers under CNCC/BGFT corridor management; Camrail to Bélabo timber terminal (SOMAC)
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: ~80% of CAR's imports; Cameroon customs values transit on the route at ~CFA 55bn/year; transit delays of several weeks reported
corridors.projects: CAR moved its transit customs window from Douala to the Béloko dry port (finalised 6 Apr 2026); CNCC Garoua-Boulaï truck hub opened Sep 2025; AfDB Transport Facilitation Programme (2007) asphalted Garoua-Boulaï–Bouar (154 km) and Ngaoundéré–Garoua-Boulaï (260 km) and financed joint border checkpoints
corridors.notes: Security-driven: convoys escorted by MINUSCA/FACA inside CAR; the Kribi–Bangui variant is promoted by PAK. Kentzou–Gamboula is the secondary crossing.

corridors.name: Camrail Douala – Yaoundé – Bélabo – Ngaoundéré railway (Transcamerounais)
corridors.route: Douala (Bessengue/port) → Eséka → Yaoundé → Bélabo → Ngaoundéré; branches Douala–Nkongsamba and Mbanga–Kumba
corridors.length: ~1,000 km network (Douala–Yaoundé 265 km; Yaoundé–Bélabo 293 km; Bélabo–Ngaoundéré 329 km); metre gauge
corridors.operator: Camrail (concession signed 19 Jan 1999, operations from 1 Apr 1999; reference shareholder Africa Global Logistics/ex-Bolloré; State minority)
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: 1.8m t freight and 1.7m passengers (2014); recent tonnage n/a; Ngaoundéré terminal 1,350 TEU capacity
corridors.projects: World Bank-financed rehabilitation and signalling of the Douala–Yaoundé line (USD 368m component; preliminary design studies delayed, bidding expected 2025); Ngaoundéré platform rehabilitation; PIDA-listed Douala–Ngaoundéré–N'Djamena rail extension to Chad (studies)
corridors.notes: Competitor asset: AGL (MSC group) controls Camrail as well as KCT and the Douala timber yard, giving MSC an integrated port-rail chain to Chad. Eséka derailment (2016) and ageing track constrain speed/capacity.

corridors.name: Yaoundé – Douala motorway (phases 1 and 2)
corridors.route: Yaoundé (Nkolbisson) → Bibodi → Bodmon → Edéa → Pitti → Douala (Massoumbou)
corridors.length: Phase 1: 60 km (Yaoundé–Bibodi); phase 2: 141.1 km in 5 sections (Bibodi–Bodmon 39.5 km, Bodmon–Edéa Est 34 km, Edéa Est–Ouest 30 km, Edéa Ouest–Pitti 18 km, Pitti–Massoumbou 19.5 km)
corridors.operator: Ministry of Public Works; contractor China First Highway Engineering Corporation (CFHEC)
corridors.capacity_or_traffic: n/a (parallels the congested N3 that carries most Douala port hinterland traffic)
corridors.projects: Phase 1 (~CFA 350bn, works 2014-2022) open; phase 2 (~CFA 880bn / ~USD 1.5bn, Chinese financing sought at FOCAC 2024) launched Oct 2024 with 36-month schedule, government target 2028
corridors.notes: Critical for Douala–Yaoundé truck flows to Chad/CAR corridors; phase 2 also links to the Edéa–Kribi motorway at Edéa.

corridors.name: Kribi – Lolabé motorway and Edéa – Kribi motorway
corridors.route: Kribi port (Mboro/Lolabé) → Kribi → Edéa (junction with Douala–Yaoundé motorway)
corridors.length: Kribi–Lolabé 38.5 km (+4 km port access), open since 2022; Edéa–Kribi ~92 km planned (total 108 km, 2x3 lanes, 110 km/h)
corridors.operator: Ministry of Public Works; contractor China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC); PPP with Chinese partner for operation/tolling
corridors.projects: Edéa–Kribi section costed at CFA 512.3bn (CFA 482.6bn works), Chinese-financed, with 4 interchanges and 5 major bridges (Nyong 225 m, Lokoudjé 200 m); Kribi–Lolabé section built 2015-2022 with China Eximbank financing
corridors.notes: Without the Edéa link, Kribi port traffic to Douala/Yaoundé still uses the two-lane N7 — a major constraint on Kribi's hinterland reach and a driver of feeder traffic to Douala.

corridors.name: Bamenda – Mamfe – Ekok/Mfum – Abakaliki – Enugu corridor (Cameroon–Nigeria)
corridors.route: Bamenda → Batibo → Mamfe → Ekok (CM) → Mfum (NG) → Ikom → Abakaliki → Enugu; feeder Kumba–Bachuo Akagbe (150 km)
corridors.operator: Ministries of Public Works (CM) and Works (NG); AfDB-financed
corridors.projects: AfDB Transport Facilitation Programme (ADF loan UA 90.4m approved 25 Nov 2008; EU grant EUR 25.5m): road upgrade, 402 m Cross River bridge at Ekok–Mfum (68% complete Apr 2020, since opened) and joint border post; Mfum–Ekok Border Modernisation Initiative launched 10 Sep 2026 (OSBP assessment, data exchange) with AfDB, ECOWAS, ECCAS, Afreximbank, AfCFTA Secretariat
corridors.notes: Main formal road link between CEMAC and Nigeria; traffic depressed by the Anglophone crisis in Cameroon's North-West/South-West regions since 2017.

corridors.name: Mbalam/Nabeba – Kribi iron-ore railway
corridors.route: Mbalam (CM) / Nabeba (Congo) iron-ore mines → Kribi mineral terminal
corridors.operator: n/a (mine developers; Sundance Resources' earlier concession terminated)
corridors.projects: Standard-gauge line reported under construction in 2025; PAK plans the associated mineral terminal from 2027
corridors.notes: Would make Kribi a bulk-export port; progress historically slow and dependent on iron-ore financing.

border_crossings.name: Kousséri – Nguéli bridge (N'Djamena)
border_crossings.traffic: Main gateway for Chad's imports on the Douala–N'Djamena corridor (~79% of Chad's imports transit Cameroon); truck counts n/a
border_crossings.projects: CNCC truck logistics base under construction at Kousséri (2025); AfDB programme financed the Kousséri by-pass, Walia–Nguéli dual carriageway (6 km, Chad side) and joint checkpoints with axle-load scales
border_crossings.notes: Single Logone bridge into the Chadian capital, congested; security context of the Lake Chad basin (Boko Haram) adds escort requirements.

border_crossings.name: Yagoua – Bongor Logone bridge
border_crossings.traffic: New second road link Cameroon–Chad; crossing time cut from ~45-60 min (ferry) to minutes; volumes n/a
border_crossings.projects: 620 m bridge (CFA 74bn; total programme ~CFA 92bn with 14.2 km access roads, customs posts) financed by AfDB loan + EUR 40m EU grant, built by Razel/Sotcocog, works from Feb 2020, inaugurated 28 Apr 2025
border_crossings.notes: Opens a southern alternative to Kousséri for the Douala–N'Djamena corridor via Maroua/Yagoua–Bongor–N'Djamena.

border_crossings.name: Garoua-Boulaï – Béloko
border_crossings.traffic: Main gateway for CAR (~80% of CAR imports); goods valued ~CFA 55bn/year by Cameroon customs
border_crossings.projects: CNCC 200-truck logistics hub opened 5 Sep 2025; CAR transit customs window relocated from Douala to Béloko dry port (Apr 2026); AfDB-financed joint checkpoint and asphalting of Garoua-Boulaï–Bouar
border_crossings.notes: Convoys escorted inside CAR; periodic closures during CAR crises (2014); refugee pressure in the East region.

border_crossings.name: Kye-Ossi (tri-border with Gabon and Equatorial Guinea)
border_crossings.traffic: Largest CEMAC land-trade hub for food exports to Gabon/Equatorial Guinea; heavily informal; three customs crossing points connected to CAMCIS
border_crossings.projects: MAGZI plans a 150 ha industrial zone at Kyé-Ossi by 2035
border_crossings.notes: UNECA survey (Mar 2026): high clearance costs, unreceipted charges (83% of traders), delays (78%), informal payments (56%); Equatorial Guinea periodically closes its side; border closed Aug-Sep 2016 during Gabon's election.

border_crossings.name: Abang Minko'o – Eboro
border_crossings.traffic: Cross-border market whose main customers are Gabonese; road link Ambam–Bitam–Oyem–Libreville
border_crossings.notes: Multiple checkpoints/informal levies reported on the approach; closed with Kye-Ossi during Gabon's Aug-Sep 2016 election.

border_crossings.name: Ekok – Mfum (Cross River bridge)
border_crossings.traffic: Main formal road gateway between Cameroon and Nigeria; volumes n/a; officials acknowledge flows 'less efficient than expected'
border_crossings.projects: 402 m two-lane bridge and joint border post (Nigerian side) financed by AfDB/EU under the Bamenda–Enugu programme; Mfum–Ekok Border Modernisation Initiative launched 10 Sep 2026 (joint OSBP operations, real-time data exchange, joint risk management) backed by AfDB, ECOWAS, ECCAS, Afreximbank and AfCFTA Secretariat
border_crossings.notes: Access road from Mamfe/Bamenda affected by the Anglophone conflict; joint border post built but unified operations still being negotiated.

border_crossings.name: Kentzou – Gamboula
border_crossings.traffic: Secondary CAR entry point (Berbérati axis); mainly regional/informal trade
border_crossings.notes: Was inaccessible in 2014 due to anti-Balaka activity; used as a fallback when Garoua-Boulaï is disrupted.
